candidates.review_text:
I like this place a lot.  It is pretty no-nonsense, though it doesn't skimp, either in terms of vibe or food.

I went here this past Saturday night with a large group (11).  They don't take reservations, so we had to get seating on the fly, which sucked but should have been a sign for the large group to just go elsewhere.  Seating was predictably somewhat of a problem, though I would not blame the staff for this - they are just not really equipped for this, which is their prerogative.  (The customer is not always right.)  The gang had to sit at the bar for awhile while some space cleared.  They have this policy of shortening the tables late at night because they want more space for the dj/standing crowd, which meant that we were a little limited in choosing seats.  We ended up getting split into two groups at tables next to one another, which was lame, but, again, predictable since they aren't really made for large groups.  Though it was not really her fault or anything, the waitress helping us with this mess got the birthday boy a cake on the house, which was a very nice gesture and not necessary at all.  It was a pleasant ending to a situation that was not really ideal for anyone involved.

As for the food, it is pretty tasty and dynamic.  I usually get a burger, but  that night I bought the calamari and the steak/fries appetizers.  Both of them were solid.  Friends ordered the veggie burger (great), corndog (good), soup (ok), creme brule (not so good)... well, I don't really know what the other table ordered, so I'll leave it at that.

In brief: the great food, solid vibe, they have Yuengling for $2.50, just don't come here with a large group late on a Saturday night.

Oh yeah, and the exterior is beautiful and the interior design also looks quite good.

Wow!! Impressive food and service! 

Was packed/busy. We had reservations for 6 for dinner.

Never been so was a great first time experience. All wait staff and food staff were very attentative and friendly. 

Great for large groups, it's a huge restaurant. 

Pretty much loved everything that was offered.

Came in with a group of 20ish people a little after the new year and it was great! We dined family style, and the food was very promptly brought out, and each of us had enough to eat (plus almost everyone took a to-go container or two, or three, as well). All the food was delicious (and the to-go containers even had reheating instructions, very helpful).

The stand out experience though was when someone poured a drink on me before walking out (due to the conversation, not the food)- the server was RIGHT THERE with a handful of napkins to dry off with, I was very impressed! And they were also very patient as my party collected the payment from everyone as well, which was quite an issue with 20+ people. Great place for large groups.

A BYO surprisingly close to Penn's campus that isn't filled with Penn kids?! Crazy.

The first time I came here, about a year ago, really late on one of the first few days of spring. I got the lamb chops which exceeded my expectations. What I really remember is that it was my friend and I's first time trying hookah-our waiter went above and beyond showing us exactly how to do it! (So, if you haven't tried hookah and are curious, why not try it here?) Even though it was late, we never felt rushed either. 

I've since come back multiple times with groups of 8+ and I feel like it's an excellent choice for a group that size. The least adventurous can get the grilled chicken while others aren't stuck. In the 4+ times I've been here, I can't remember anyone disliking any dish they got. Service is also pretty quick-no waiting around a check, which I appreciate. Also in the plus side, there is more than enough space for large groups and it's easy to hear people, even at the height of their dinner crowd on a Friday or Saturday.

This is my favorite, go-to sushi place in Center City. I live nearby in Center City and often end up here with friends, ready to house enormous amounts of sushi. The menu has variety, plus many of the sushi nigiri items that I go for (I'm a big fan of saba nigiri and ikura nigiri, the mackerel and the salmon roe.) The proximity to other places in the 'hood is a major appeal of this place. It is fantastic, except when there are large groups of students or girls playing with their hair and having boring conversations about shopping while pretending to eat. Sometimes some of these people drift over from Rittenhouse and find themselves at a table that instead should belong **TO ME**, not them(!), because I love this place and how cozy it is and want it all to myself! This place is pretty small, with just a few tables and a 3-person sushi bar, and this is part of the charm. It does not have a lot of room, and although the staff is very accommodating, it would probably be hard to seat a group larger than four in this place.

I was part of a group who had reserved the upstairs room for lunch after a conference in the morning. There were probably around 30 of us, but we dribbled in over the course of maybe e 20 minutes; we didn't arrive en masses.  I was with the stragglers. I loved the rustic old-style architecture, the casual décor., the very interesting menu, and the great selection of craft beers.  I think we were ordering from the brunch menu (it was a Saturday), and I had huevos rancheros, which was delicious. However, the service was disappointing. It seemed that the server either was not aware that we were a group, or the server didn't know how to serve a large group. Instead of waiting for the whole group to arrive, she took orders as people came in. This meant that some received their food while others were still waiting for theirs. When I arrived, and the server came to me, I asked if orders were being taken for drinks or food. The server said "You can order whatever you want." :-\ I ordered a craft beer (21st amendment brew-free-or-die IPA was great!) and huevos rancheros (delicious!) . The beer arrived, but my food was delayed long after everyone else's. The server said it was "sent to a different table, and I would be getting another order soon." So, I had to wait even longer, and started to eat while others were finishing up. This all made for a confusing eating experience. I would definitely visit Strangelove's again for the great food, beer, and ambiance, but I would suggest some training for staff who serve large groups.

The details listed above are for their OLD LOCATION. At their NEW LOCATION AT THIS ADDRESS, they have tons of space! It's GREAT FOR GROUPS, they have WAITER SERVICE, TAKE RESERVATIONS and it's BYO. If you bring tequila, they'll hook you up with salt and some awesome margarita mix. 

I had a party of 12, called a few days in advance, and they accommodated both us and several other groups in their dining room that same evening. The ambience is relaxed, the waiters were attentive without being bothersome and the food was, as always excellent. Best of all, we felt comfortable hanging out for hours and no one bothered us. AND they don't have TV's and keep the music fairly low - we could all actually hear each other but since it's so group friendly we didn't feel like we were bothering anyone if we did get a little loud. 

Highly recommended for groups!

Very, very cool spot.  Large and spacious to accommodate friends in the double digits!  That, for me at least, is the biggest selling point because most other spots aren't really designed to sit down large groups of people on the fly, i.e. last minute-- whereas the layout of this spot allows it.  The food was ok, not spectacular- and drinks were solid.  Overall, the atmosphere carries this place.  Now i haven't been dancing here... but i liked the bar/dinner part enough to give it a try.

This review is only for the hot pot. 

Finally tried Emei for hotpot after hearing about it from friends for such a long time! We got the half and half pot (but as with most half and half situations, the nonspicy half usually gets contaminated half way through, oh well b/c I like spicy, but careful if you don't!)

What I liked about this place is that you can order individual items from the menu. Portions are smaller (and in the $4 range), which is perfect, because you can order as you go. We got most of the traditional things that you may (or may not) want in your hot pot: beef, lamb, potatoes, winter melon, enoki mushrooms, fish balls, beef balls (with filling!), tofu, frozen tofu, leafy greens (lots of different kinds!), vermicelli, spam, fish tofu, beancurd skin among lots of other things I can't remember. 

We had a table of 8, and after about 6 plates of beef (and all of the above mentioned), we were stuffed, and the total was about $20-25 per person (after tip and tax and with soft drinks!), which is really decent for hot pot!! (vs the $45 post tip tax w/o soft drink per person that Jane G charges!!!) This will be my new hot pot spot if I'm craving it and not feeling like making it at home. 

Some good to knows: The fatty beef is really fatty - each slice is half fat. The lamb is not sliced frozen lamb that you may expect (it's fresh and cut in strips, not what I'm used to but not bad). There are ~3 sauces to choose from (sesame oil, sesame paste, or satay sauce) - when they say sesame paste, that's exactly what you get (naive me thought it would be some great mixed sesame sauce, nope, add your own soy sauce etc. for flavoring). Great for large groups - there's a "party room" in the back with 2 large round that tables, which could fit appx 20 people.

this is the first time i've wanted to write a review in ages, but xi'an sizzling woks deserves all of the good press the have received. well-cooked and delicious food, decent setting/ambiance and a much expanded (and printed menu) from their opening days. have tried a few things on the menu and am whole hog in love with the dumplings in sour broth. absolutely delicious on a cool (er) night in july and i'm sure this dish will be amazing in the official cooler weather. noodles are lovely not overdressed, dry sautee green beans are my third favorite accompaniment to any meal (behind broccoli rabe and water spinach) and xi'an does them well. am looking forward to eating my way through the menu and i wish them success!

n.b. - i selected the cheap price range below since a bowl of the dumplings in sour broth could EASILY fill up anyone and comes in at $8.50. my dining companion and i rung up a $40 bill, but we ordered five dishes and took home half of the food....also, not super good for groups - they have two standard 8 seaters, but it is a long and narrow building, so super large groups won't work well here (they can probably push the 8-seaters together though if you time it right).
Despite the tip that they were not good for groups they were very accommodating to my party of 12. The service was prompt and polite and the food was excellent for the price

delicious food, very generous proportions, flavorful, pleasant customer service and fun atmosphere.

this is a good spot for large groups (4+) as the service is swift (from my experience) and polite.

their noodle dishes could do no wrong, in my opinion.

enjoy.

My family and I went there for the first time and we were very excited about it. Everything was so fresh and delicious! We enjoyed the choices of meat and seafood as well as vegetables, they had a great variety and they definitely don't skimp you on anything so for the price it's definitely worth it just depends on how hungry you are or how much you can eat because it's VERY filling!

It's a really neat place and the sauce bar is a great touch. The place isn't ginormous but it's spacious enough. We made reservations and still waited about 20 minutes to be seated but thats going to happen because this place seems like it's always packed so if you have a big party or just to be safe, definitely call ahead and make your reservation. 

Overall, the place is very clean, the atmosphere is nice, it's great for groups and they have private rooms as well for bigger parties. 

I just wish the grill was bigger and would get a little bit hotter but it really just depends on how big your group is and how much you have to cook on it obviously. 

I can't wait to come back!

Tldr: Popular and affordable malaysian restaurant with flavorful curries that is great for family style with 7 - 10 people! 

Food! Cause its the most important: We went family style and started with the roti canai because there were so many great reviews. The appetizer was delicious but I would say mainly the curry which I would recommend putting of your subsequent dishes. Of note, the roti canai comes as one big pancake making it not the easiest to share, but doable. Next, we had the thai basil noodle, which was very savory and had a collection of meat options (Shrimp, chicken, etc). Then came the Green Nasi Lemak, which was flavorful but was made even better by the addition of the roti canai's curry haha. Lastly, we had the mixed vegetable in the clay pot because we saw it all over the restaurant and it didn't disappoint. It probably was barely enough for a group of 6, but I would say the best part of that dish was also the curry flavor. 

Menu: I personally don't have a strong grasp on the variety typical of malaysian restaurants, but the menu appeared to be fairly exhaustive with several different meat and vegetable options. 

Environment: There are about 3-4 large round tables that can seat around 10 people which makes this place great for large groups. The rest of the seating appears to be in 2 - 4 person arrangements. There isn't really a good waiting area and the restaurant doesn't seat until all members are present so if you are meeting a group. I would plan on meeting and all entering at once. 

Service: there were numerous staff moving throughout the restaurant but we had to ask mulitple to get water and rice during our meal =\

Cost: Our meal ran us around $58 so with 6 of us that came out to around $10, which was bad at all.

Charming spot that reflects some of the architectural warmth of the Dandelion pub down the street. Had a group dinner on the second floor - big homey dining room, well-padded parlor chairs, and a nice bar. Service was great. Meat and fish dishes disappeared from everyone's plates. Slight disappointment was the much-lauded fried chicken... skin was less crisp, and met less moist, than the best chicken, but sauce and sides were fine. If you're looking for a nice dinner event space, I'd certainly recommend for a lively (sharp acoustics) group dinner of 20 or so people.

Delicious food, fast service & great for large groups.
I came here on a whim with a group of 7 people on a Sunday afternoon - around 1pm.
We were able to get a table immediately. Food came quickly, tea pot was always full & the staff here are always lurking around if you need anything. Everything was delicious - do I need to go into details?

Really good, fancier, healthy bar/restaurant. It has a nice industrial feel, with a really cute large outdoor patio outside. We sat upstairs which is big and open. There were quite a few older business type people from navy yard and the sports complex, as well as young professionals. All the food was seriously delicious, there is a large salad section, sandwiches and entrees. The salads are all unique and seasonal. I really loved the peach and tomato salad, as well as the fig appetizer toast. Oo the froze is also a must if you like wine and frozen margaritas! Finally for dessert we tried 3 of the 4 options. My favorite was definitely the rice pudding which definitely tasted like it had condensed milk (aka the best milk). Others liked the little fried dough with Nutella dip. The s'mores sundae was ok. Overall it was a really nice experience, especially for large groups so definitely recommend!

I went here for my birthday (was the birthday girl reviewer Samantha M referred to!) and was extremely pleased!  The place was very busy and although there was occasional waiting for a server, overall I felt we were taken care of.  We had a group of 12 and although there was (warranted) concern by the owner that not everyone would show up, I found him attentive but sufficiently patient.  If my restaurant were that busy, I'd have been worried too!  I'd been looking for a BYOB, Italian restaurant with good food and within walking distance of places to go out.  I found just that!  My food (a rigatoni and sausage dish) was wonderful and most of my party enjoyed their meals as well.  We got appetizers to share (calamari and prosciutto) and I was very happy with both.  The garlic in olive oil for the bread was outstanding.  I'm not a tiramisu person, but even that was good and it was so nice of the restaurant to bring us free desserts!   

I liked that we could talk freely without feeling like we were disturbing others.  I didn't feel that it was too loud and with as many bottles of wine as our party had, I wouldn't have wanted a very quite place!  I thought this was a great restaurant for groups, and clearly many other parties thought so too because there were three other large groups in there that night.  i would definitely go back.  If I could rate this a 4.5 stars, I would have.  My only complaint was perhaps that it was a little tight for those of us sitting against the wall, but this wasn't a huge deal to me.  I had a wonderful birthday dinner and would recommend this place for sure!

The food is great but if you are dining to also enjoy a having a conversation with someone, go elsewhere. This restaurant routinely welcomes very large groups who bring lots of wine and drink way too much. The large groups of young folks have on three separate occasions (!!) been obnoxiously LOUD and rowdy. The restaurant management takes no action. Will not return because it feels like a frat house and not a restaurant. Too bad - good food but horrible experience

NOT recommended for large groups. 

I was eager to try this place after several recommendations. I made a reservation for 12 for a celebration gathering.  From the moment we walked in, we felt rushed out the door.  Among the first words the server said before we even sat was "I have another group coming in at 8:30 so..." It put a timer on the whole evening. 3 in our group were running a little late and we would've liked to wait for them to start but our server basically let us know "it's now or never"  We didn't finish each course, and there was no offer to pack up the leftovers so into the trash it went, which is a shame because the food was great!  The rushed pace of the meal was completely at odds with the otherwise relaxed and lush atmosphere.  The table we sat at was extremely tight for 12 people, I can chalk that up to the intimate atmosphere but I would totally understand other large groups feeling claustrophobic and packed in. 

Another thing, this business is CASH ONLY. Nowhere on the menu or the website that hosts it, nor during the calls I made to ask a few questions and then make the reservation, nor during the servers "has anyone eaten here before" introduction was this ever mentioned. Again, with a smaller group that may not have been so bad but with a check of almost $400 that I was trying to treat the group to, it's embarrassing to it leave everyone scrambling to throw in enough cash to cover it.

I would potentially return here with a much smaller group.  If they can only offer a  rushed experience which leaves guests feeling like an afterthought, then they never should've taken our reservation.

Horrible service for good but overpriced Chinese food.  I had takeout from here once prior to dining in the restaurant and it was good but I did find it to be more expensive than other Chinese restaurants. When planning a holiday gathering with colleagues, we decided on Han Dynasty because it was a BYO and the gentlemen who we spoke with on the phone had assured us they could accommodate our group of 12.  When we arrived they had us at 2 separate tables, we were promised one table for our group.  We waited for some time but no one brought us menus, we had to go get them ourselves from the hostess stand. Our tables were not set either.  We also had to ask for ice and glasses, and our server seemed rather annoyed by this request. Throughout the meal our water was never freshened and once our ice was gone that was it.  It took forever to finally get our orders in, then food started randomly coming out family style but no one informed us we'd be served that way.  Oh yeah and even though they brought out or food family style we had to ask for plates to eat off of. We got doubles of some of the food we ordered...they just kept bringing the same things out, then when it came time for the check they never brought it and when we eventually got it there were a lot of mistakes.  Clearly they can not accommodate large groups well. This place is a hot mess that cant function when they're in the weeds.  For what they charge they really should get their act together.

I will start out by saying that I enjoyed my food and it's a BYOB, that's pretty much the only two good things I have to say. 

I came with a large group and we had an 8:30 p.m. reservation. When part of group arrived early, they were told our tables would be ready shortly. I arrived close to our reservation time and there was a lot of confusion. There really isn't a good waiting area, especially for groups and the hostess asked someone from our group to wait between the doors. Most of group went outside, even though it was kind of chilly and three of us waited in the middle of the restaurant (where others were waiting). She came back up to us and said that she needed us to wait outside or between the front doors, which was a small area. No other large groups that came were asked to wait outside.

When 9:15 p.m. rolled around, we went back in to ask if she had an idea when we would be seated. She said they were working on it and I asked for the true story of how long it would be. She told us they were short staffed. We were finally seated around 9:30. We had to ask the wait staff for menus and for bread several times. We were pretty quick to order once they finally came around to take the order- but our food didn't come out until after 10:30. 

It's hard to even review the food since the rest of the experience was so terrible but I had the Gnocchi, which was very delicious. The Primi item was enough food for a dinner. 

I won't be back and I would skip this restaurant especially if you have a large group.

Was here for a private event and experienced atrocious service, bad enough that I would not go back.

Their website touts their ability to handle large groups for private events... but they were completely unprepared to handle the group. Service was extremely slow, and our server was rude as well. From ordering to receiving food took at least 40 minutes. When one person's food came out (missing an item), we asked the server when we could expect the other food and received a rude and unhelpful response of "It's a small kitchen." No refills were offered on coffee. One food order came out a good 15 minutes before the others. Getting the attention of the server was nearly impossible.

The food itself was adequate--nothing special, but nothing wrong with it. The "maple syrup" described in the menu was pancake syrup rather than actual maple syrup (which is fine... just don't call it maple syrup if it's not!).

We were also charged for an item we didn't order and it was an ordeal to get the attention of the server to get it removed from the bill, and no apology was offered when we pointed out the mistake.

Overall, very unimpressed. They clearly weren't prepared to handle the group and seemed to fell no need to apologize for their lack of preparation.
NOT ACCOMMODATING TO LARGE GROUPS!!!! Do not go if group is 6 or more! Forgot about us for 2 hours even though we went up every 20 minutes to check in. Manager was rude and did not care.

Came here for our group farewell dinner. Mind you, we were a group of 50, but it took FOREVER to go through the courses, a salad, dinner and desert.  I have been to other restaurants where they served large groups and they manage to keep the meal moving. The staff were not on top of it. Did not offer drink refreshments to include water. I had to walk up to the bar where all waitors and waitresses stood talking and laighing amongst themselvs to ask for more water.  The staff knew they already had their gratuity so they didn't even try. Waters were not refilled at all during the meal.  Although the food was tasty, it was cold. To top it off, when we went to leave, a Vietnam Veteran in our group who is sick went to step down the curb at the wheelchair accessible access as to not step down the curb step and the valet honked at him to get out of the way. How rude and disrespectful.  This man had a cane and you cannot wait, when you are getting paid for an elder, a Veteran in fact to move safely towards the bus? I am so ashamed at what I just witnessed.  Would NOT recommend this place nor will I return.

Max Brenner would be good if you go for the right things. The two whimpy stars I gave deserves explanation. I only gave it 2 stars, One for the hot chocolate in a hug mug which was probably the best Ill ever have and I actually bought the hug mugs online for my brothers as x-mas gifts (which went over very well). Then one for the chilli chocolate waffle fries, original and yummy.

As for the other 3 missing stars they go to poor waiters, bad entrees, and cramped inside. Went there with the fiance and families around the holidays last year about 10 of us, and they seated us by the bar which means people kept bumping into our chairs and the waiter spilled a hot chocolate shot in my lap, which they didnt even have the manners to comp. The entrees tasted like TGIF on an off night with dryn burgers and over seasoned fish tacos. None of the entrees were memorable and all over priced.

The decor is one of a kind but its just not made for large groups or a great dinner. If you go here, just get anything with  chocolate and maybe an appetizer, anything else will dissappoint.

Went here for the first time for a large party (10+) this weekend and 2 stars is generous...

We were told ahead of time for large groups pre-fixe was required ($40 a person) and parties over 6 must pay cash (even though smaller parties take card). A strange request, but reviews here and from friends have been amazing (have heard it's cheap and delicious) so I was expecting we'd throw down for $40 (pre tax and tip).

The appetizers were underwhelming - Greek salad and a hummus/dip plate with pita, and then it was time to order. Options were chicken kebob, lamb gyro, shrimp & rice, or a veggie pasta. Everyone was less than enthralled with the entrees that came out. They were fine, but like, $5 food truck fine. Even worse, when we looked at the menu afterwards if we had just ordered the same apps and entrees it should have been less than $20 a person.

There must be a huge difference in quality between small groups and large ones. I'd assume for bringing a large group in you'd either get the same level of service or some discount, not get ripped off. 

It pains me to leave nasty reviews, but with places like Kanella down the street take your large parties there for better quality and priced Greek food.

Ok so this review is ONLY for the double fried wings! Hands down the best wings in town! The wait was far longer than the person informed me of when I placed my order over the phone, gave them an extra 10 minutes on top of the 35, my orders still were not ready.. but if your patient.. please do get the wings... the place is kinda cute..a little much for my taste.. the decor is a little "loud"... the staff were friendly... but seemed out of sorts with the mild volume of folks that day.. 

Ok so went back here for a friends birthday. Jan 12, They do not reserve for large groups so she had to go early to hold the table, ok, and so they apparently are not familiar with tending to large parties, the smaller sized parties had far more attention from their servers than our group of 10, and speaking of server I could not tell you one name, of the 3 different ones that came to the table, ok, so the service, welp, not much to mention. They should hire a few more servers for the weekend and focus on small party sizes. The service was horrible that evening, I waited for a curry chicken with rice meal for 45-50 minutes... and it left a lot to be desired once it had arrived. Their Chicken wings are still the best i've tasted in Philadelphia. And the service is the worst I've experienced thus far...

The people were incredibly nice and the service was top notch. It's also a really nice large space. Great for groups. 

The food was a solid meh. The mac and cheese was grainy, the brisket and pulled pork were bland. The sausages were VERY good though.

Have given it a few tries, and have not been impressed. The outside dining area is fun for large groups meeting for drinks. The food and lack of service are disappointing. In Fishtown for the night, go somewhere else, there are plenty of choices.

This little place is very pretty inside, and the staff were friendly. The food was not special even though the menu looked interesting. I got a waffle which had no decorations and just cut-up pieces of banana on it. No butter was served with the waffle. My friend got an interesting mound of eggs and some ham which looked skimpy in the middle of an otherwise empty plate. My iced tea was served without sugar or sweetener. When I asked for some, I was handed two Equals (no container of choices), and my friend had to make a separate request for sugar. He received a container with a spoon in it. He asked for cream and was handed three small separately wrapped cream containers. 

At a breakfast restaurant where you pay 2 or 3 dollars for drinks, the restaurant shouldn't be so cheap as to hand out individual servings. Lots of us use more than three of those tiny cream containers.

My other major complaint was the background music. A few selections were fine (solos, soft etc) but music that involve large groups of singers or drummers and bands  disrupts the dining experience and makes it hard to hear conversations. This was extremely distracting.

I won't be going back.

This place was awful for brunch.   We were sat in a small room with 2 large groups and a couple with a baby.   The baby was very well behaved but the noise level from the two large groups in such a tiny space made the experience horrible.   Add to that tasteless food and horrible service and you have the recipe for never returning.

Had a very bad experience coming here for the first time. We had a group of 7 and called in advance to see the wait. They said 20 minutes, but we ended up waiting over an hour and had to split our group into 2 tables. Our waiter forgot to take our order, forcing us to grab him from the server station, and after taking our order, never revisited our table to check on us or refill our water. We sought the help of a waitress not assigned to our table when we needed something. 

Tables that ordered after us got their food before we did, and when our food finally came, it was not as we ordered it or advertised. They forgot our sides. Also, apparently a salad with "poached eggs and bacon" means a singular poached egg with half a piece of bacon chopped up on top. When I asked for more eggs, as advertised on the menu, they charged me. I also would not recommend this dish. It was average.

I'm not sure if they were understaffed or if the service was just poor, but this was definitely a sub par dining experience at best. Would not recommend.

Regretfully, we chose to eat at your establishment last night before attending a show at the local theatre. We had a group of ten and we made reservations. The service was extremely poor. We were handed two menus for ten to share, no napkins or silver ware until requested. Our drinks sat empty for several minutes and our food didn't arrive for about an hour after ordering.  When our meals finally arrived, we had to rush to eat to make our show. We made reservations at 5:15pm for a 7:30pm show. This should have been ample time to have a nice comfortable meal. Its a shame that a center city establishment located in the theatre district directly down the street from the biggest theatre in Philadelphia couldn't accomodate a party of ten with prior made reservations. Extremely disappointed.

Hotel is huge if you like that. Downside is they host large groups. I am here tonite with a group of 2500 of the most inconsiderate people I have ever seen in public. Here on business and completely infuriated at this point and tired of fighting crowds of jerks. Reached out to manager who told me there was nothing he could do. Called the Marriott platinum line and got moved to another hotel - thats the right answer rookie. Here on business once a month or so, would never again stay at this place. So much for platinum treatment if you are in the way of their huge group sales. Management is a joke, why wouldn't you tell your platinum business travelers they are in for a nightmare????  Avoid at all  costs !

I've been for dinner a few times there and overall it's just kind of blah. It's nice for large groups because it's spacious and they have nice outdoor seating during the summer, but it's nothing to write home about. There are way better places in Manayunk to spend time and money for dinner.

prompt:
你正在为餐饮评论召回系统建立逆向评测集。输入是同一个固定特征下的一批真实 Yelp 完整评论。

当前固定特征：group_suitable
中文含义：从不适合多人聚餐到非常适合
